⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Because it smelled like burning rubber before the brush stopped, this is a safety hazard. Please stop using the vacuum immediately and do not plug it in again until a qualified engineer has inspected it. The most likely cause is that the drive belt snapped or the brush motor overheated and failed while trying to turn a jammed brush bar. While I can't make it safe for you to use, if you want to see what happened, you can unplug it (or remove the battery) and check the floorhead: look at the brush roller to see if it's tangled with hair or threads, and check if the rubber belt is still intact around the pulleys. However, given the burning smell, this needs professional attention.
